processing: The Guangxi cultivar is used for green tea, as is typical of its area: fixed, rolled and dried. In northern Guangdong the same name covers teas made with sun-withering and pan firing.
harvest_season: An early-sprouting plant, so spring picking comes early; spring one-bud-two-leaf shoots are the standard reference for it.
appearance_dry: Green rolled leaf, typical of regional green tea made from a larger leaf.
appearance_liquor: Clear yellow-green, as is typical of the class.
appearance_wet: Soft green leaf, on the larger side.
taste_profile: Described in general terms as fresh and clean in aroma with a mellow, sweet taste.

brewing.notes: Around 85°C in a glass works; shorten the steep if the larger leaf turns bitter.

vintage_note: Little is recorded about specific trade practice. As usual for green teas, expect the current year's crop and drink it within a year. Check the place on the pack, because tea from northern Guangdong uses the same name.
description:
Yaoshan means Yao mountains, and the name is used in more than one place. Here it mainly means Yaoshan Zhong, a local tea plant from the Dayao mountains at Miaohuang in Xiangzhou, Guangxi. Similar names also appear on teas from Ruyuan in northern Guangdong.

The plant is a seed-propagated, shrubby, large-leaf, early-sprouting type, rated as cold-hardy and suited to making green tea, and recommended for Guangxi's green tea areas. So the leaf itself is better described than any finished product.

Finished teas are described only in broad terms, with a clean aroma and a mellow, sweet taste. Brew it like a green tea at around 85°C, and treat the larger leaf gently.

Because the name is shared, ask where it was grown. A Guangxi Yaoshan and a Ruyuan Yaoshan may have little in common beyond the mountain name.
history:
Little is documented about this tea's early history. The Dayao mountains at Miaohuang are given as the origin of the plant, with a long but undated history of cultivation by the Yao people, for whom tea was used in hospitality and traditional remedies.

In more recent years, branding has focused on Ruyuan in northern Guangdong, where the name has been developed commercially.
